articles.title: Nvidia, AMD, Dell sink in global tech rout on AI funding worries
articles.preview: AI-related stocks experienced a significant downturn this week, with a combined loss of over $1 trillion. Concerns about financing for massive AI infrastructure projects are driving the sell-off across the global tech sector.

summary.t: A wave of selling pressure impacted global tech stocks. Twenty of the most valuable AI and semiconductor companies lost over $1 trillion this week. Nvidia, AMD, and Intel experienced declines, while Micron saw a slight increase. Additionally, stocks in South Korea, Japan, and Europe also fell significantly, impacting companies like SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics, SoftBank Group, and ASML.

Investors are worried about the rising cost of financing large-scale AI infrastructure projects. Broadcom and Intel executives have warned that financing challenges could hinder the AI boom. Rising U.S. Treasury yields above 5% are exacerbating these concerns. The Nasdaq Composite, S&P 500, and Dow Jones Industrial Average all experienced declines on Wednesday and Thursday.

Concerns over a potential memory chip oversupply in 2029 are also contributing to the market downturn. Manufacturers are ramping up production, and China's CXMT announced a breakthrough in memory density, signaling increased competition. Elon Musk predicted significant RAM production in China by 2028.

Despite the sell-off, some analysts remain optimistic. Dan Ives believes the pullback presents a buying opportunity, arguing that underlying demand for AI computing power remains strong. He emphasizes that a change in demand, rather than interest rates, would alter his view.

articles.title: Apple and Meta team up to make Muse AI model run on Mac computers
articles.preview: Apple and Meta are collaborating to allow developers to run Meta's Muse Spark Open AI model on Mac computers. This marks a surprising shift in the rivalry between the two tech giants.

summary.t: After years of competition and strained relations, Apple and Meta are partnering to enable the use of Meta’s Muse Spark Open AI model on Mac computers. This collaboration is being spearheaded by John Ternus at Apple and Meta’s AI chief, Alexandr Wang. The move represents a significant change in the Silicon Valley landscape, following a period of animosity following Apple’s privacy changes in 2021.

The Muse Spark Open model is an 816-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model designed to run locally on Mac Studio PCs. Users can utilize between two and four Mac Studio PCs to perform tasks like coding, video analysis, and agentic work. The model’s local operation enhances security and reduces user costs. Apple’s Mac Studios, particularly those equipped with the M5 Ultra chip and 256GB of memory, are crucial for running this model efficiently.

Currently, a Mac Studio with the M5 Ultra chip and 256GB of memory costs at least $10,799. A more expensive version with 512GB of RAM will be released later this month. Developers can download the AI model from websites like Hugging Face without extra configuration, and Apple has optimized the model for faster performance on its hardware using its MLX AI framework.

Meta’s collaboration with Apple extends beyond just Muse Spark Open. The company has purchased hundreds of Mac computers for its Superintelligence team to experiment with local AI and agents. This partnership aligns with Meta's broader strategy of leveraging open-source AI, a point of contention in Washington. Apple’s recent partnerships with OpenAI and Google further demonstrate its growing involvement in the AI space, although some integrations have faced challenges.

articles.title: TSMC chip capacity is ‘fierce’ battleground for AI customers, amid record quarter
articles.preview: TSMC is facing intense competition for manufacturing capacity due to the surging demand for AI chips. The company’s record quarter highlights this struggle, with limited supply impacting the entire industry’s growth potential.

summary.t: TSMC is experiencing unprecedented demand driven by the artificial intelligence boom. The company’s record quarter demonstrates this, with analysts describing the competition for manufacturing space as ‘extremely fierce.’ TSMC can’t produce chips quickly enough to meet current needs, creating a bottleneck for the industry’s scaling potential. Jordan Klein, a Mizuho Securities analyst, noted that companies are vying for leverage and supply. TSMC currently serves over 534 customers, with the top 10 accounting for 78% of its net revenue.

A wide range of tech giants, including Apple, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and OpenAI, rely on TSMC for custom AI accelerators. Sajiv Dalal, TSMC’s North American CEO, reports receiving at least 10 calls daily regarding wafer capacity. Long-standing relationships are crucial; companies like D-Matrix, with over 20 years of collaboration, depend on TSMC for processor manufacturing. Individuals like Jerry Qubain, who has visited TSMC since 1992, play a central role in facilitating these partnerships.

TSMC is aggressively expanding its manufacturing capacity with planned fabs in Taiwan, Japan, and Arizona. The company’s total investment commitment now stands at $265 billion, with an additional $100 billion planned for Arizona. TSMC is also considering a new fab location in Texas. The company is utilizing existing factories with ASML’s extreme ultraviolet lithography machines to increase output. SEMI projects 102 new chip fabs globally by 2029, with significant growth expected in Asia, particularly China.

Despite TSMC’s dominance, competitors like Samsung and Intel are being considered as alternative sources. Analysts suggest companies are seeking a second source to maintain competitive pricing. By 2029, American fab investments are projected to more than double. With the ‘extremely fierce’ competition and expanding capacity, TSMC is considered strategically positioned for the future.

articles.title: AWS, Anthropic race to deploy army of specialized engineers key to proving AI spending will pay off
articles.preview: Big Tech companies are investing heavily in specialized engineers to demonstrate the value of their AI investments. Several companies are deploying these engineers, known as forward deployed engineers (FDEs), to help businesses integrate AI technologies and achieve tangible results.

summary.t: Multiple tech giants are committing billions of dollars to build a workforce of forward-deployed engineers (FDEs). Amazon Web Services (AWS) has pledged $1 billion, OpenAI is investing over $4 billion, and Anthropic is dedicating $100 million to train 10,000 FDEs by 2027. Accenture and Google Cloud are also building a combined 1,000-person FDE team.

These FDEs combine AI and software expertise with an understanding of business operations. They work directly with customers to translate promising AI experiments into usable applications, navigating technical, security, and organizational challenges. The role requires more than just technical skills; engineers must also possess strong customer empathy and judgment to handle unexpected problems.

Demand for FDEs is surging, with job postings increasing dramatically from under 200 in 2023 to over 7,300 in the first nine months of 2026. Median advertised salaries have risen sharply, reaching $195,456 – more than three times the average U.S. job posting salary. Consulting firms like Deloitte and Accenture are major recruiters in this field.

Companies are employing diverse strategies to develop deployment expertise. AWS is building its own FDE organization, while OpenAI is acquiring Tomoro and Anthropic is training engineers through its Claude Frontier Academy, modeled after medical education. Accenture and Google Cloud are retraining software engineers for this role, with onboarding taking 30 to 90 days.

While early deployments show productivity improvements, concrete financial returns from AI investments remain elusive. Some case studies, such as those involving PennyMac and Smarsh, demonstrate increased engineering efficiency, but independent verification of financial gains is lacking. The success of this expanding workforce will ultimately determine whether AI investments deliver the expected returns.

articles.title: Teaching students to think and learn through questions
articles.preview: Duolingo is releasing a new resource for teachers in Brazil. This resource uses AI and focuses on helping students learn through questions.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang urges U.S.-China dialogue on 'potentially dangerous' AI
articles.preview: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang believes a U.S.-China dialogue is crucial for managing the risks of rapidly developing artificial intelligence. He argues for collaboration with Chinese AI companies to ensure the technology’s safe advancement.

summary.t: Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, stated unequivocally that the company must collaborate with Chinese AI firms. He emphasized the need for this partnership to proactively monitor and mitigate the ‘potentially dangerous’ risks associated with the technology’s development. This stance directly contrasts with calls for increased regulation from organizations like OpenAI and Anthropic.

Earlier this year, in September, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and his Chinese counterpart He Lifeng discussed a potential ‘U.S.-China AI dialogue.’ This dialogue would include a channel for reporting incidents up to a ‘national security level.’

During the meeting, Chinese President Xi Jinping indicated that despite potential competition, China and the U.S. could ‘cooperate even more’ in the field of AI. Both nations agreed to continue dialogue, exchange views on risks and benefits, and jointly prevent misuse of the technology.
Huang suggested the U.K. could play a key role in facilitating these dialogues, leveraging the country’s ‘intellectual capital.’ He believes this is essential for advancing AI safety globally.

articles.title: Deutlicher Gewinnsprung: Chip-Riese TSMC setzt Höhenflug fort
articles.preview: TSMC, der weltweit größte Auftragsfertiger für Chips, hat seinen Gewinn erneut gesteigert. Der Chipriese profitiert maßgeblich vom aktuellen Boom der künstlichen Intelligenz.

summary.t: TSMC hat im vergangenen Quartal einen Rekordgewinn von rund 21,02 Milliarden Euro erzielt, was einer Steigerung von 69 Prozent entspricht. Diese Zahlen übertrafen die Erwartungen der Analysten, die mit einem Ergebnis von rund 500 Millionen Euro gerechnet hatten.

Um dem steigenden Bedarf zu begegnen, plant TSMC Investitionen von bis zu 52 Milliarden Euro in den Ausbau seiner Produktionskapazitäten. Ein Großteil dieser Investitionen, rund 265 Milliarden Dollar, soll in einem neuen Werk in Arizona erfolgen.

TSMC erwägt den Bau einer weiteren Anlage in Texas, möglicherweise durch Anmietung eines Teils der von Elon Musk geplanten „Terafab“-Fabrik. Das Unternehmen ist ein wichtiger Partner für Nvidia, Apple und AMD.
TSMC spielt eine Schlüsselrolle im KI-Boom, da es die Chips für führende Unternehmen wie Nvidia und Apple fertigt. Zavier Wong von eToro bezeichnet TSMC als 'im Zentrum des KI-Ökosystems'.

articles.title: Anthropic's third-quarter revenue is said to hit $16.8 billion ahead of IPO
articles.preview: Anthropic announced record third-quarter revenue of $16.8 billion, fueling anticipation for its upcoming IPO. The company is also reporting profitability and positive cash flow.

articles.title: An update on independent evaluators
articles.preview: Anthropic is taking significant steps to increase transparency and safety in its AI model development. The company is partnering with independent evaluators, including METR, to conduct rigorous risk assessments and bolster accountability.

summary.t: Anthropic has committed to stronger independent evaluation of its models and safety practices. This includes joining the White House Accord on Super Intelligence and collaborating with multiple third-party auditors. Currently, they are working with METR, SecureBio, and Accenture as evaluators.

Anthropic has granted METR, a nonprofit evaluator, employee-like access to its systems. Six METR employees have been provided with company hardware, office space, and access to internal tools. They will publish the results of their risk assessments, focusing on areas like incidents and practices.

Anthropic recognizes the need to protect commercially sensitive information, such as compute or training data. They’ve established clear guidelines for information sharing, restricting access to specific categories and allowing redactions where necessary. METR can publicly comment on these redactions.

Anthropic is developing a tiered system for evaluator access, starting with narrowly scoped investigations and progressing to full publication rights. SecureBio is currently in the first tier, reviewing a specific risk report. The goal is to eventually have multiple teams at the third tier, publishing their own analyses.

Anthropic is also pursuing partnerships with Accenture and Faculty, focusing on model evaluation, red-teaming, and alignment assessments. These partnerships are still in early stages, with evaluators receiving limited information and publication rights.

articles.title: OpenAI sued by 8 states over ChatGPT safety concerns
articles.preview: Eight states have initiated lawsuits against OpenAI due to concerns about the safety of its ChatGPT chatbot. The lawsuits allege the chatbot poses risks to children and deceives parents.

summary.t: Eight states – Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho, and Montana – have filed separate lawsuits against OpenAI. Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird stated the lawsuit aims to protect Iowans from OpenAI’s alleged dangerous and unlawful conduct. These legal actions are being pursued in individual state courts.

The lawsuits center on claims that ChatGPT is unsafe, particularly for children. Specifically, the states allege the chatbot provides dangerous medical advice, encourages violence, and promotes suicide. Several wrongful death lawsuits have also linked ChatGPT to harmful delusions and suicide attempts.

OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri defended the company’s efforts, stating they’ve implemented age-specific protections within ChatGPT. The company also highlighted its collaboration with states to develop industry-wide policies. They’ve launched a dedicated ‘ChatGPT for Teens’ experience with educational features and safeguards.

OpenAI is facing increased scrutiny regarding its safety practices and has taken steps to enhance features, including parental controls and age-appropriate model protections. The company launched ‘ChatGPT for Teens’ in August, aiming to provide a safer learning environment for adolescents. Resources are available for those experiencing suicidal thoughts; the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is 988.

articles.title: Bank of America hired 1,000 contractors to patch software flaws exposed by Anthropic's Mythos
articles.preview: Bank of America has hired a large number of contractors to address security vulnerabilities identified by AI. The bank is investing heavily in remediation efforts following the emergence of advanced AI models.

summary.t: Bank of America brought in 1,000 contractors during the second quarter to address software flaws. Additionally, the bank already had 3,000 personnel working on this issue. This effort was triggered by the release of Anthropic’s Mythos AI model.

The bank allocated ‘a couple hundred million plus’ to software remediation and related regulatory issues. They are anticipating savings of $300 million this year, rising to $700 million by 2027, from approximately 130 internal AI projects.
Bank of America reduced its workforce by approximately 3,400 employees, representing roughly 5% of its management team. The impact of AI on this reduction is currently unclear.

articles.title: Marktbericht: Europa wertvollster Konzern ASML macht KI-Boom möglich
articles.preview: ASML, Europas wertvollster Konzern, hat einen enormen Umsatzanstieg verzeichnet. Dieser Erfolg ist maßgeblich für den aktuellen KI-Boom verantwortlich und hat die Aktie auf den höchsten Stand seit ihrer Gründung gebracht.

summary.t: ASML meldete einen bemerkenswerten Umsatzanstieg von knapp 11,7 Milliarden Euro im aktuellen Quartal. Der Gewinn stieg auf fast fünf Milliarden Euro, was die Erwartungen der Analysten übertraf. Die Bruttomarge verbesserte sich um 3,5 Prozentpunkte auf 57,5 Prozent.

ASML stellt die hochmodernen Lithografiemaschinen her, die für die Produktion von KI-Halbleitern unerlässlich sind. Ohne diese Maschinen wäre der aktuelle KI-Boom nicht möglich. Die Maschinen werden für große Chiphersteller wie Apple, Nvidia und Samsung eingesetzt.

Die Nachfrage nach ASMLs Produkten übersteigt das Angebot bereits für 2027 und 2028. Christophe Fouquet, Firmenchef von ASML, plant, die Kapazität für 2028 um über 30 Prozent zu erhöhen und prüft Möglichkeiten, die Kapazität weiter zu steigern. Kunden haben bereits Bestellungen für 2029 und 2030 aufgegeben.

Der DAX erholt sich und liegt bei über 25.400 Punkten. Die Aktie von ASML steigt um rund drei Prozent. Experten sehen einen 'Abwarte-Markt' aufgrund von Unsicherheiten bezüglich des KI-Booms, hohen Ölpreisen und der Zinsentwicklung.

articles.title: Anthropic urges court in Washington, DC, to rehear appeal of Pentagon blacklisting
articles.preview: Anthropic is challenging the Pentagon’s decision to blacklist its AI models, citing concerns about retaliation and constitutional rights. The company is seeking a court to rehear its appeal of the blacklisting decision.

summary.t: In March, the Pentagon, led by Pete Hegseth, labeled Anthropic, an American AI company, a ‘national-security supply chain risk.’ This followed a breakdown in negotiations regarding the military’s use of Anthropic’s Claude AI models, specifically concerning mass surveillance and lethal autonomous warfare.

Initially, a divided panel of the D.C. Circuit Court upheld the Pentagon’s blacklisting in September. Subsequently, a San Francisco federal judge ruled in August that the DOD had violated Anthropic’s First Amendment rights and that the supply chain risk designation constituted illegal retaliation.

Despite a $200 million contract signed in July 2025, negotiations regarding Claude’s deployment on the GenAI.mil AI platform collapsed in September. Anthropic argues the blacklisting was a response to the company’s advocacy for AI safety.

Both sides have declined to comment on the ongoing litigation, with Anthropic’s representatives stating the court ignored evidence of retaliation and the DOD spokesperson stating the agency does not comment on pending litigation.

articles.title: Lange Haftstrafe droht: OpenAI-Mitarbeiter wird wegen eines versteckten Abhörgeräts festgenommen
articles.preview: Ein OpenAI-Mitarbeiter wurde wegen des Einsatzes eines versteckten Abhörgeräts festgenommen. Die Behörden sehen darin eine Bedrohung für die nationale Sicherheit.

summary.t: Ein 35-jähriger saudischer Staatsbürger, Abdulrahman A., wurde am 9. Oktober festgenommen. Die US-Bundespolizei FBI ermittelt in dem Fall, nachdem das Gerät am 30. September in einem Konferenzraum von OpenAI entdeckt wurde. Es war in einen USB-Anschluss eines Fernsehers versteckt und mit Toilettenpapier gewickelt.
Das Abhörgerät, welches verschlüsselt war, wurde am 30. September entdeckt. Es wurde zwei Tage zuvor dort angebracht.

Ein zweites Abhörgerät wurde in einer Tasche gefunden, die A. in den Firmenräumen zurückgelassen hatte. Zudem wurden Anfragen zu Aufnahme-Vorrichtungen über einen Chatbot-Account der Ehefrau des Mitarbeiters festgestellt.
Bei einer Verurteilung drohen Abdulrahman A. bis zu fünf Jahre Haft und eine Geldstrafe von bis zu 250.000 US-Dollar.

articles.title: Finnland: KI-Boom auf Kosten der Natur?
articles.preview: Google plant ein Rechenzentrum in Finnland, das massive Investitionen von 13 Milliarden Euro erfordert. Die Rodung von über 300 Hektar Wald zur Errichtung des Zentrums hat jedoch zu erheblichen Bedenken hinsichtlich der Umweltauswirkungen geführt.

summary.t: Google plant ein Rechenzentrum in Muhos im Nordwesten Finnlands. Mehr als 300 Hektar Wald wurden gerodet, um die Fläche für das Rechenzentrum zu schaffen. Die Rodung erstreckte sich über eine Fläche von über 400 Fußballfeldern.

Die finnischen Behörden haben die Arbeiten gestoppt, da wichtige Voraussetzungen wie eine Umweltverträglichkeitsprüfung, Genehmigungen und ein Bebauungsplan fehlten. Die Vorsitzende des finnischen Naturschutzbundes, Hanna Halmeenpää, kritisierte die Rodungen scharf.

Die Freilegung des Waldbodens birgt Risiken für die Umwelt, da Böden Wasser versauern und Schadstoffe in Flüsse gelangen könnten. Google hat sich für die Vorgänge entschuldigt und eine Überprüfung der Situation angekündigt.

Der Bürgermeister von Muhos, Kimmo Hinno, sieht im Rechenzentrum große Chancen für Arbeitsplätze und wirtschaftliche Entwicklung. Google plant insgesamt 13 Milliarden Euro in Finnlands digitale Infrastruktur zu investieren, aufgrund günstiger Bedingungen wie niedrige Temperaturen und Strompreise.

articles.title: Preparing for the 2026 US midterms
articles.preview: This news article details Anthropic’s ongoing efforts to ensure Claude is a reliable and unbiased tool for users, particularly as it relates to the upcoming 2026 US midterms. The company is focusing on preventing misuse, providing accurate information, and continuously improving the model’s fairness and safety through various evaluations and safeguards.

summary.t: Approximately 5.75% of conversations on Claude.ai currently involve politics, public policy, or social issues. A significant portion, around 0.51%, directly relates to elections and voting. Notably, users rarely ask Claude for specific voting recommendations, instead seeking information to form their own opinions, such as understanding candidate stances on issues. The company estimates that only 0.01% of conversations involve direct requests for votes. As the midterms approach, this percentage is expected to rise, and the company is actively monitoring these trends.

To combat misinformation and provide users with accurate details, Anthropic is integrating reliable information directly into Claude’s responses. They’re partnering with Democracy Works to display TurboVote links for voter registration and polling place information. Claude will also draw official voting data from Democracy Works for users in the US, offering state-specific answers without requiring users to leave the conversation. Furthermore, Claude will provide up-to-date election results on election night and in the following days, directly within the conversation.

summary.h: Focus on Fairness and Bias Mitigation
summary.t: Anthropic is committed to ensuring Claude’s responses are unbiased, with its latest models, Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5, scoring 99% on political evenhandedness evaluations. The company is actively testing and refining these evaluations, employing independent groups like the Future of Free Speech, the Foundation for American Innovation, and the Collective Intelligence Project to assess Claude’s responses. These evaluations revealed that Claude rarely refused requests, but sometimes added unsolicited counterarguments, and Sonnet 4.5 was found to be less evenly balanced in its responses to left-leaning prompts. To address these issues, Anthropic is improving how Claude handles yes-or-no questions and shorter answers, and refining its approach to adding caveats.

Anthropic is deploying automated classifiers to detect election-related abuse, and has partnered with the Institute for Strategic Dialogue (ISD) and the McCain Institute to pressure-test these safeguards. Analysts identified that while Claude reliably refused single harmful requests, it could miss malicious campaigns spread across multiple requests. The company is adding new classifiers to detect novel misuse, including attempts to build fake social media accounts or news sites. They’ve also strengthened their cyber protections for election infrastructure and campaigns. Anthropic is actively investigating and preventing coordinated abuse around elections, including instances where foreign actors used Claude to produce biased news coverage. The company’s Usage Policy prohibits deceptive voting practices, and they are regularly updating it to reflect evolving capabilities and feedback. They are monitoring a broader trend of AI being incorporated into political influence operations, and proactively stopping these efforts before they reach the public.

articles.title: Anthropic opens Singapore office and signs MOU with the Government of Singapore
articles.preview: Anthropic is establishing a new office in Singapore and forming a partnership with the Singapore Government. This collaboration focuses on advancing responsible AI development and deployment within the region.

summary.t: Anthropic has opened its fifth Asia-Pacific office in Singapore. The company signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Singapore Ministry of Digital Development and Information. Kai Fong Chng, Permanent Secretary, and Ben Mann, Anthropic co-founder, formalized the agreement alongside Josephine Teo and Michael Sellitto.

The MOU outlines cooperation in AI safety, security, and model evaluation. Anthropic plans technical exchanges with Singapore’s AI institutions. They will share research, including the Anthropic Economic Index, and offer policy expertise to support Singapore’s AI development.

Claude is already being used by numerous Singaporean organizations, including GovTech Singapore, Grab, DBS, GIC, and Sea. Over 1,500 engineers at GovTech Singapore utilize Claude Code. The Cyber Security Agency of Singapore is exploring Claude’s potential for cyber defense.

Singapore ranks second globally in Claude.ai usage relative to population, with nearly six times the predicted usage. Grab’s sales assistant powered by Claude saves 40,000 hours quarterly. Supabase is building with Claude Code, and DBS is leveraging Claude across its operations. Anthropic hosted a Builder Summit in Singapore, bringing together over 300 developers.

articles.title: The EU’s next chapter in AI is agentic
articles.preview: The European Union is seeing a significant rise in the adoption of agentic artificial intelligence. This trend is poised to unlock greater value for businesses, both large and small, across the EU.

articles.title: CoreWeave credit default swaps hit distress levels as investors sour on AI debt
articles.preview: CoreWeave's financial distress is escalating due to investor concerns about its substantial AI-related debt. This has led to a dramatic increase in credit default swap spreads, signaling heightened risk perceptions.

summary.t: CoreWeave has accumulated over $51 billion in debt to finance its AI infrastructure. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 reached 15.78% as investors reacted to concerns about AI overspending and the company’s debt levels.

The spread on CoreWeave’s five-year credit default swaps rose dramatically, peaking at nearly 1,140 basis points. This represents a 16% week-over-week increase and a 164% jump compared to a year ago, indicating a significant increase in perceived risk.

The concerns surrounding CoreWeave’s debt have spread to other neocloud stocks, including Nebius and Iren. Additionally, shares of Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices experienced declines following the broader sell-off in South Korean chip stocks.

A spread level of 1,000 basis points or above is generally considered a sign of credit distress. Oracle’s five-year CDS spread also spiked this week, reaching 282 basis points, a 10% increase in one week. Investors are questioning CoreWeave’s ability to generate sufficient cash flow to cover its significant investments.

Despite the market concerns, CoreWeave maintains a backlog exceeding $100 billion, with a significant portion secured from investment-grade companies like Microsoft, Meta, IBM, and Caterpillar. However, analysts caution that the arrival of these cash flows is uncertain.
Jim Reid warned that this situation could trigger broader issues in other AI-related names, citing the potential for a downgrade from CoreWeave’s BBB rating to pressure investors into forced sales.

articles.title: Marktbericht: DAX vom Tech-Ausverkauf kaum betroffen
articles.preview: Der DAX schloss heute leicht im Plus, obwohl es einen Tech-Ausverkauf weltweit gab. Die Ölpreise und Sorgen um Staatsschulden beeinflussten den Index.

summary.t: Der DAX schloss bei 25.382 Punkten, was einem Anstieg von 0,33 Prozent entspricht. Der Index pendelte weiterhin um die Marke von 25.000 Punkten.
Ein weltweiter Ausverkauf von Tech-Aktien führte zu Verkäufen. Besonders betroffen waren Halbleiterwerte.
Die schwachen Asiakurse und die Sorgen um Staatsschulden in der Eurozone trugen zur Volatilität bei. Die hohen Ölpreise spielten ebenfalls eine Rolle.
Der taiwanesische Chip-Auftragsfertiger TSMC meldete einen Gewinnrekord im dritten Quartal mit umgerechnet 21,2 Milliarden Euro.
Hohe Inflationsdaten aus den USA, insbesondere aufgrund hoher Energiepreise, schürten die Sorge vor weiteren Zinsanhebungen der Federal Reserve.
Die US-Notenbank wird am 27. und 28. Oktober über den weiteren Zinskurs beraten. Eine weitere Anhebung ist möglich.
Am US-Anleihemarkt gibt es Zeichen einer Entspannung, die sich an der sinkenden Rendite widerspiegelt.
Die Technologiebörse Nasdaq verlor am Mittag Ortszeit rund 1,8 Prozent.
Der Dow-Jones-Leitindex legte hingegen moderat um 0,3 Prozent zu.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Techwerte-Ausverkauf juckt Dax nicht sonderlich
Viele Kurse fallen immer weiter: Ausverkauf von Tech-Aktien an US-Börsen vernichtet Billionenwerte
articles.preview: Die US-Börsen erleben einen massiven Ausverkauf von Technologieaktien. Die Stimmung ist durch Unsicherheiten über die KI-Finanzierung und steigende Zinsen getrübt.

summary.t: Der Dow-Jones Index notierte am Morgen 0,3 Prozent höher bei 51.755 Punkten. Der S&P 500 verlor 0,6 Prozent auf 7672 Zähler. Der Nasdaq Index fiel um 1,4 Prozent auf 26.309 Punkte.
Der Philadelphia Halbleiter Index verzeichnete Einbußen von über zwei Billionen Dollar an Börsenwert nach sieben Verlusttagen.
Chiphersteller TSMC gab aufgrund makroökonomischer Unsicherheiten eine vorsichtige Prognose für das Jahr 2027 bekannt.
Anleger bezweifeln zunehmend, dass sich die Investitionen in KI auszahlen werden. Das defizitäre Unternehmen CoreWeave verlor zwei Tage in Folge sieben Prozent.
Der Start der neuen Rakete Neutron von Rocket Lab wurde auf 2027 verschoben, aufgrund von Problemen mit den Treibstofftanks. Der Start könnte sich bis ins zweite Quartal 2027 verzögern.
Aktien des Agrarchemiekonzerns FMC brachen nach einem trüben Ausblick um 34 Prozent ein, mit Aufwendungen von 625 bis 675 Millionen Dollar.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Abseits des Tech-Booms: Diese Aktien haben Potenzial
articles.preview: Die Technologieaktien, insbesondere im Bereich KI und Chips, erleben derzeit Turbulenzen. Dennoch gibt es laut einer Fondsmanagerin interessante Anlagealternativen jenseits des aktuellen Tech-Booms.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Nasdaq mit knallrotem Start
Der Börsen-Tag: "Blase geplatzt?" - Chip-Höhenrausch folgt der Kurskater
Furcht vor einer Insolvenzwelle: Tech-Ausverkauf erfasst Europas Börsen
articles.preview: Die europäischen Aktienmärkte erleben derzeit einen erheblichen Ausverkauf im Technologiesektor. Dies wird durch steigende Zinsen und Zweifel an der Rentabilität von KI-Investitionen verstärkt.

summary.t: An der Frankfurter Börse sind vor allem Infineon, Aixtron und Suss Microtec unter Druck. Die Aktien dieser Unternehmen brachen um acht bis neun Prozent ein. Die Nervosität der Anleger wuchs nach den überraschend hohen US-Verbraucherpreisen. Der europäische Technologie-Branchenindex verzeichnete einen Verlust von drei Prozent.

Auch in Japan und Südkorea fielen die Technologieaktien deutlich. Der Nasdaq in den USA verzeichnete einen Minus von knapp zwei Prozent. Die Anleger befürchten eine massive Korrektur und sehen die hohen Bewertungen der Technologieaktien kritisch.

Die Kosten für die Absicherung gegen Insolvenzen von Rechenzentren sind gestiegen. Anleger bezweifeln die Rentabilität von milliardenschweren KI-Investitionen. Die Credit Default Swaps auf Oracle verteuerten sich um 26 Basispunkte. Die Stabilisierung am Öl- und Anleihemarkt verhinderte jedoch größere Kursverluste.

Der Dax fiel um rund ein Prozent auf 25.173 Punkte. Der EuroStoxx50 verlor rund ein Prozent auf 6133 Zähler. Der Preis für Brent-Öl sank um rund 1,5 Prozent auf 104,54 Dollar pro Fass. Die Regierung von US-Präsident Trump erwägt, Sanktionen gegen die Schattenflotte zu lockern.

articles.title: Marktbericht: TSMC gibt sich keine Blöße
articles.preview: TSMC hat einen neuen Rekordgewinn erzielt. Die Nachfrage nach Halbleitern, insbesondere im Zusammenhang mit dem KI-Boom, ist weiterhin extrem hoch.

summary.t: Der taiwanische Chip-Auftragsfertiger TSMC hat einen Umsatz von 41,66 Milliarden Euro erzielt, was einen Anstieg von 50 Prozent gegenüber dem Vormonat darstellt. Dieser Erfolg ist vor allem auf den anhaltenden KI-Boom zurückzuführen, der die Nachfrage nach Chips in allen Bereichen der KI-Wertschöpfungskette stark erhöht.

TSMC erwartet ein Wachstum des Umsatzes um 44 Prozent für das Gesamtjahr 2026 und plant eine Beschleunigung des Wachstums auf 55 bis 61 Prozent für das laufende Quartal. Das Unternehmen bekräftigt sein Investitionsziel von 64 Milliarden Dollar.

Um der hohen Nachfrage gerecht zu werden, plant TSMC den massiven Ausbau seiner Produktionskapazitäten. Der Konzern bestätigt sein Investitionsziel von 64 Milliarden Dollar, um die Anleger zu beruhigen.

Trotz der beeindruckenden Zahlen der Börse bleiben die Zweifel bestehen. Der Nasdaq und der Kospi erlitten erhebliche Verluste, was auf die Sorge vor steigenden Zinsen und die finanzielle Abhängigkeit von Tech-Unternehmen zurückzuführen ist. Auch der DAX reagierte negativ auf den Tech-Ausverkauf.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: DocMorris hebt erneut Prognose an
Memory stocks are getting hammered. China and a 2029 oversupply are the big worries
articles.preview: Memory chip stocks are experiencing a significant downturn, driven by concerns about Chinese competition and potential oversupply. This is happening amidst broader market volatility.

summary.t: Several memory chip stocks, including SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron, have fallen sharply. This decline is fueled by the emergence of ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) in China, which is developing a new memory product with higher storage density. Analysts are questioning CXMT’s ability to scale production and capture market share.

Multiple sources, including analysts Kevin Cassidy and Ben Barringer, believe that CXMT’s new technology will not significantly alter the existing supply-demand balance. A forecast of a 2029 oversupply, highlighted by Professor Hwang and Ahn Ki-hyun, suggests a potential ‘red ocean’ market condition.

Elon Musk’s prediction of a large increase in RAM production by China in 2028 adds to the concerns. Counterpoint Research forecasts a DRAM price decline of around 23% in 2028 compared to 2027, but a significant increase from 2025 levels. The industry is entering a ‘New Normal’ era with longer-term agreements.

Demand for memory chips is increasing due to the AI boom and the growing use of memory in Nvidia chips. While manufacturers are expanding capacity, it will take 3-5 years for new factories to come online. Investors are assessing whether the traditional boom-and-bust cycle is changing, with a focus on Long-Term Agreements (LTAs) to mitigate price volatility.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: TSMC arbeitet an Kapazitätsgrenze - Gewinnsprung vermeldet
TSMC posts record profit for a sixth straight quarter, beating estimates on AI boom
articles.preview: TSMC has achieved record profits for a sixth consecutive quarter, driven by strong demand for AI chips. The company’s performance significantly exceeded analyst expectations, signaling continued growth in the semiconductor industry.

summary.t: TSMC announced a record third-quarter profit, marking a 68.7% surge compared to the previous year. This represents the sixth consecutive quarter of record profitability for the world’s largest contract chipmaker.

The company’s operating margin reached 58.7%, surpassing its own guidance. TSMC forecasts fourth-quarter revenue between $52.3 billion and $54.3 billion, reflecting a 14% sequential increase and a 58% jump year-on-year.

TSMC anticipates significantly higher capital expenditure from 2026 to 2028 to support growing customer demand. The company is also constructing a second fab in Arizona, with expected mass production beginning in the third quarter of 2027.

Demand for advanced chips, particularly 7-nanometer and more advanced technologies, accounts for 79% of TSMC’s revenue. High-performance computing and smartphones are key revenue drivers, with automotive experiencing the fastest growth at 23% quarter-on-quarter.

articles.title: Sorge wegen hoher Inflation: Tech-Werte rutschen an der Wall Street ab
articles.preview: Die US-Verbraucherpreise sind deutlich gestiegen, was zu Sorgen an der Wall Street führt. Die Angst vor einer baldigen Zinserhöhung der Fed belastet vor allem Technologieaktien.

summary.t: Der Nasdaq-Index erlitt am Dienstag einen großen Verlust. Er sank um 1,9 Prozent und erreichte den größten Tagesverlust seit Ende Juli, wobei er auf 26.693 Punkte fiel.

Die US-Verbraucherpreise stiegen im September stärker als erwartet, mit einer Jahresinflationsrate von 3,7 Prozent. Dies hat die Wahrscheinlichkeit einer weiteren Zinserhöhung der Fed auf 37 Prozent erhöht.
Insbesondere KI-basierte Technologieunternehmen erlitten erhebliche Kursverluste. Oracle fiel um 8,8 Prozent, während Coreweave und Nebius um 15 bzw. 10 Prozent abstürzten.

Auch andere Aktienmärkte waren betroffen, darunter Bank of America, die um 4,8 Prozent fiel, und Dell und Hewlett Packard Enterprise, die ebenfalls deutlich an Wert verloren. Bending Spoons stieg jedoch um 41 Prozent aufgrund einer Investition von Berkshire Hathaway.

articles.title: Traders pile into 'bubble puts' on CoreWeave as neocloud stocks plunge
articles.preview: Traders are aggressively betting against CoreWeave, a key AI infrastructure provider, as its stock price drops dramatically. This surge in ‘bubble puts’ indicates a significant concern about the health of the artificial intelligence trade.

summary.t: Shares of CoreWeave experienced a sharp decline of 15% on Wednesday, following rising debt yields backed by Nvidia. This decline coincided with a broader downturn in neocloud stocks, including Nebius Group and Iren, which fell by as much as 10%.

Trading volume for options on CoreWeave, Nebius, and Iren spiked dramatically, reaching levels more than seven, four, and two times their 30-day averages respectively. Notably, traders heavily favored purchasing put options on CoreWeave, driving a purchase of nearly 200,000 puts.

A significant trade occurred around 10 a.m. ET involving the purchase of 26,000 37.5-strike puts expiring December 18th for $1.9 million. This was a new position, representing a substantial increase in open contracts from just over 1,000.

Industry experts, like Scott Bauer of Prosper Trading Academy, described these trades as ‘bubble puts,’ suggesting they are not primarily designed for forced liquidation but rather for hedging exposure or engaging in margin plays within the AI sector.

articles.title: CoreWeave shares tumble as bond yields near 15% on concern about AI borrowing binge
articles.preview: CoreWeave's stock and bonds experienced a significant drop due to investor concerns about technology companies’ heavy borrowing for artificial intelligence projects. Bond yields have risen sharply, reflecting increased risk aversion.

summary.t: CoreWeave’s debt yields have surged dramatically. The 9.625% bond due in 2032 now carries a yield of 14.8%, while the 9.75% bond due in 2031 is at 14.9%. Investor demand for risk compensation has increased, driven by concerns about the scale of AI-related borrowing.

Analysts point to CoreWeave’s balance sheet as a contributing factor to the market’s reaction. Paul Meeks of Freedom Capital Markets noted that CoreWeave has taken on more debt and is building more data centers than its peers. The company’s credit rating is currently a B+ – considered junk bond territory – and is expected to report flat margins from June to September.

The concerns surrounding AI borrowing have impacted the broader tech sector. Shares of Oracle fell nearly 9%, with its 6.25% bond yielding 7.24%. The Nasdaq Composite closed down 1.9% on Wednesday, reflecting wider market anxiety.

Large tech companies, including Alphabet, Amazon, Meta Platforms, and Oracle, have collectively issued over $228 billion in bonds this year – more than double the amount issued in the entire year of 2025. JPMorgan estimates these hyperscalers are set to spend over $800 billion this year, and over $1 trillion annually by 2027.

articles.title: Dell stock plunges 11%, leading data center sell-off as fears mount about 'enterprise AI timing'
articles.preview: Dell stock experienced a significant drop, and several other data center companies followed suit. Concerns are rising about the timing and volume of enterprise investment in artificial intelligence.

summary.t: Dell shares fell by 11% on Wednesday, impacting Hewlett-Packard Enterprise (HPE), Oracle, and Super Micro. Barclays downgraded ratings for Dell, HPE, and NetApp, citing concerns about enterprise AI spending.
Wall Street’s optimism regarding AI infrastructure has diminished. Revenue figures from OpenAI and fears of rising interest rates are contributing to this shift.

The memory chip market is experiencing a downturn, highlighted by progress at CXMT and declines in Micron (-11%), SK Hynix (-13%), and Western Digital (-8%). This is impacting infrastructure companies’ revenue.
Barclays analysts estimate that only approximately 25% of total enterprise AI spend is directed towards hardware. They also note that businesses are allocating only 5% of their IT budgets to AI.

articles.title: Inflation data, Bank of America's penalty, Apple's new home hub and more in Morning Squawk
articles.preview: Inflation data is set to be released this morning, with economists anticipating a potential acceleration in price growth. Simultaneously, Bank of America faces a significant penalty from the U.S. Treasury Department, impacting its earnings.

summary.t: Bank of America shares dropped over 4% in premarket trading following a $1.2 billion penalty from the U.S. Treasury Department. The penalty stemmed from alleged violations of anti-money laundering and sanctions laws. This resulted in a 17-cent per share reduction in income. CEO Brian Moynihan’s leadership is now under scrutiny due to the situation.

Morgan Stanley reported equities trading revenue exceeding analysts’ expectations by more than $900 million. This positive result will be discussed today with Brian Moynihan and Ted Pick on CNBC’s ‘Squawk on the Street’.

Anthropic, the maker of Claude, is scheduled to disclose its third-quarter financials to institutional investors today. The meeting at its San Francisco headquarters follows recent revenue figures from OpenAI that impacted the tech sector.

Recent polling indicates a shift in Latino voter sentiment in South Texas, potentially making them a key factor in the upcoming midterm elections. Republicans are optimistic about gaining Hispanic voter support, but concerns about inflation and immigration are impacting enthusiasm.

Apple debuted its new home hub, HomeView, priced at $299. The device features a seven-inch screen and is designed to integrate Apple devices within a household. This launch marks Apple’s first non-iPhone product under CEO John Ternus.
Attacks on Saudi Arabia’s second-busiest airport highlight increased risks in commercial aviation. Recent data shows changes in volume at the Middle East’s busiest airports.

This report was compiled by CNBC’s Michelle Fox, Chloe Taylor, Hugh Son, Leslie Picker, Kate Rooney, CJ Haddad, Justin Papp, Kif Leswing, Leslie Josephs, and Gabriel Cortes. Caleigh Keating assisted in production, and Josephine Rozzelle edited this edition.

articles.title: ASML says it's getting order interest through 2030 as profit smashes expectations
articles.preview: ASML announced strong customer interest in its lithography tools extending through 2030, and the company’s profits significantly exceeded expectations. This positive news is being closely watched by investors assessing the demand for ASML’s advanced semiconductor equipment.

summary.t: ASML reported that customers are expressing interest in placing orders for its lithography machines through 2029 and 2030. Specifically, some customers have indicated interest in orders for 2029 and even 2030.

The company’s third-quarter profit surpassed expectations. ASML now anticipates sales between 44 billion and 45 billion euros for 2026, an increase from the previous forecast of 43 billion euros. The company’s stock rose approximately 2% in early European trade, and shares have increased by 56% this year.

Currently planned supply for 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet customer demand. ASML is exploring ways to increase capacity for 2028, aiming for a 30% increase beyond the initial forecast. Samsung and TSMC have committed to using ASML’s High NA extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines.

ASML expects China sales to account for 20% of its total business. Despite challenges selling tools to China, ASML dominates the manufacturing of DUV machines. Concerns remain about China’s ability to develop its own advanced lithography technology.
